response.message:
your saves are stacked on Tokyo and thin up front, so [Kyoto](kebi://area/jp/kyoto) and [Osaka](kebi://area/jp/osaka) are where i'll fill the gaps. here's how i'd build the trip stop by stop.

---

Kyoto

nothing saved here yet, so this one's on me. Kyoto is the most traditionally Japanese of the three cities, and it rewards slowing down. The classic move is Fushimi Inari early morning before the crowds hit the torii gates, then Arashiyama for the bamboo grove and the temples along the river. Gion in the evening is worth a wander, especially on a Friday or Saturday when you might spot a geiko heading to an appointment. Nishiki Market is a good half-morning for food and atmosphere. Give Kyoto at least two full days if you can.

---

Kyoto to Osaka (the leg)

it's only about 15 minutes on the shinkansen or 30-40 on the regular train, so you can move between them easily. Nara is right on the way and worth a few hours, deer wandering around ancient temples is genuinely as good as it sounds. Easy day trip from either city.

---

Osaka

you've got one save here: [Universal Studios Japan](kebi://venue/e68f1787-c5f6-4ed6-81b1-e0296a02ecf9), which is yours from your list. a couple of things worth knowing: it's a full-day commitment, and the Nintendo World area is the draw right now. book ahead, especially for Mario Kart. beyond USJ, Dotonbori is the eating and drinking heart of the city, takoyaki and okonomiyaki are the things to try. Osaka Castle and the surrounding park is a solid morning. Osaka is generally more casual and cheaper to eat in than Tokyo, lean into that.

---

Osaka to Tokyo (the leg)

the shinkansen is the move here, about 2.5 hours. if you have time and aren't in a rush, Hiroshima is a meaningful stop on the way (it's on the shinkansen line). Heavy but worth it.

---

Tokyo

this is where your saves are stacked, so it's mostly about ordering them well.

[teamLab Planets](kebi://venue/3546d397-b212-4cb4-866a-3a87cd06c485) is yours from your list, and it needs a booked slot in advance, don't leave it to chance. [teamLab Borderless](kebi://venue/ce8d6832-b63e-4b15-8d39-50133dabbe62) just reopened at Azabudai Hills and that's also on your list, same deal with booking. if you're doing both, they're different enough to be worth it, but spread them across separate days.

[Shibuya Sky](kebi://venue/1bd47f5c-8855-4ba9-98e6-d4c6ccf6427f) is your rooftop observation deck, sunset is the slot to go for. Book that one ahead too, it sells out.

[Shinjuku Gyoen](kebi://venue/1cf8682b-9ba4-4cc1-8a07-651c8b8b7b37) is your calm morning, especially good if you've had a few intense days by then. It's a proper garden, not a tourist trap.

[Meiji Jingu](kebi://venue/d4104468-7ac7-4674-8b91-a9b1b559fcfb) is a short walk from Shinjuku Gyoen and pairs naturally into the same morning, traditional shrine, forested grounds, very different energy from the rest of Tokyo.

[The Making of Harry Potter](kebi://venue/3d3d35f0-b134-4c2b-9dc0-e34ecef0576e) is on your list too, that's out in Toshimaen, a bit of a ride from central Tokyo, so plan it as a dedicated half-day rather than tacking it onto something else.

---

the one question that changes everything: how many nights do you have at each stop? that decides whether Kyoto gets two days or four, and whether Tokyo is a sprint or something you can actually settle into.
